relevance_note: Case series of five Chinese children with HA20 and heterozygous TNFAIP3 variants, with per-patient tables: "We identified five heterozygous variants in the TNFAIP3 gene among the five children".
method_note: I read the whole paper by hand. A Python script (scratch only) cut exact table-row spans, from the row label through the patient's column, out of the Markdown lines of Tables 1-3 and assembled the JSON. Every value was typed in from my reading, and the script asserts that each typed table value equals the corresponding table cell. Column headers: Tables 1 and 2 have patients as columns 'Patient 1' to 'Patient 5' in order. Table 3 columns are 'Patient 1' | 'The case reported by Xue et al' (c.866delA) | 'Patient 2' | 'The case reported by Xue et al' (c.1243_1247delAAAAC) | 'Patient 3' | 'The case reported by Zhong et al'. The two identically labelled Xue columns are kept apart as 'The case reported by Xue et al' and 'The case reported by Xue et al 2'. YES/NO cells are read as explicit present/absent (words, not symbols); '/' cells are not reported. Tables 1 and 3 share row labels, so some short row-prefix spans occur in both tables. Previously published people with individual detail are in scope: Xue x2, Zhong, the Zhong case's mother (described as the source of the mutation, so given the same printed variant), 'ref (32) patient' (187 kb microdeletion) and 'ref Harumi et al. patient'. The Harumi patient gets no variant row because the paper names no gene or variant for that person, only 'confirmed by genetic testing'. Inheritance for the literature cases is 'not reported' (rule 8: Table 3 'de novo' and the ref 32 'de novo' come with no parental-testing statement); the own patients' 'de novo' rests on 'they have all been tested to confirm their origin'. P1/P2/P5 variants are called 'small indels' by the authors and printed with 'fs' protein notation; recorded as frameshift. Lab abnormalities (CRP, ESR, WBC, hemoglobin) were judged against the reference ranges printed in the Table 2 row labels; platelets and IL-6 were not made into features because the authors don't comment on them. Diarrhea comes from the group statement 'All five patients ... intermittent diarrhea'; 'two of the five patients experienced intermittent bloody stool' names no one and was not assigned. cohort_size_as_stated = 5; the 168-patient systematic review (ref 14) is a different study. CONTRADICTIONS: (1) MMACHC variants and MMA: the Abstract and Discussion attribute the two MMACHC variants to patient 3, but the Figure 1 legend (C, D) and the treatment section attribute MMACHC/MMA to patient 2. The MMACHC variants are left out. The MMA diagnosis and hydroxocobalamin are recorded for patient 2 only, as the treatment section states them. (2) The Table 3 column labelled 'Patient 3' carries c.133C>T: p. R45X, which is Patient 4's variant in Table 1. Its phenotype values match Patient 4 and the text's Patient 4 vs Zhong comparison, but its treatment ('Thalidomide, glucocorticoid') contradicts Patient 4's 'Thalidomide'. Because the column's attribution is contradictory, it is not used for any person. (3) Patient 2 oral ulcers: Table 1 and Table 3 say NO, the Discussion says 'patient 2 had rash, gastrointestinal ulcers, and oral ulcers'. Both rows are emitted and the checklist item is not reported. (4) Xue case 2: the text says 'no liver injury', while Table 3 gives ALT 165.6 and AST 172.9 (reference 0~40). Both are emitted. The text also speaks of Xue's 'patients' (plural) with each mutation, while Table 3 shows one case per column; one row per column, and text statements about those 'patients' are tagged 'inferred from group statement' where the table is silent. (5) Patient 1: 'severe hormone-dependent allergic reactions' during treatment vs the group statement that none of the patients reported 'any special allergies'. Both rows are emitted. (6) The Discussion gives gastrointestinal ulcers as 80%, but Table 1 has gastrointestinal lesions YES for all five and the endoscopy text describes ulcers in all five; per-person rows follow Table 1 and the endoscopy text. (7) 'All patients aged from 2 to 10 years' vs ages at genetic diagnosis of 6m and 10m: group-level, not used. (8) The Figure 1 legend prints 'NC000006.11: g.136693638138817508del' (underscores lost); the Table 1/text form is used. (9) The Table 1 row label is 'Genomic location (GRCh37/ hg19)' although most cells are c./p. notation. The transcript NM_006290.5 from the Table 1 note is given only for the four c. variants, not for the Table 3 literature variants.
